legend.heading: What the colored labels mean

state_law.label: State law does not allow this
state_law.line: A Florida law takes the subject away from counties. Shown for comparison only.

legend.passing: Passing the test only means an item is not ruled out. It does not mean the item is lawful in a given county, wanted by whoever would receive it, agreed to by a developer, or worth a set amount.

homes.name: Standards
homes.line: Every project must meet the county's standards.

homes.name: County item
homes.line: The county can charge an impact fee, or use a development agreement, to cover what is needed to handle the impacts its own impact study measures, such as backup power at county facilities.

homes.name: County land lease
homes.line: On land the county owns, the county also sets the rent: cash rent at full market value, with rent paid in kind possible on top.

homes.name: Private agreement
homes.line: Other benefits, such as computing time or training seats, can come only from a private agreement between the developer and a community group. The county is not a party to that agreement.

counts_note: The 36 items and the 11 that State law does not allow were counted again on 18 November 2026 from the Screen's source at this commit: its filters read All 36 and Not allowed in Florida 11, and its 36 cards carry 11 State-law labels. The Core project confirms them with its release of the record.

items.name: Emergency power for county facilities
items.vsub: Only as mitigation the county's impact study supports
items.hnote: Mitigation, sized by the county's impact study. Nothing is delivered from the project site.
items.evText: Model text written; not yet reviewed by a lawyer
items.lead: If the grid goes down for days, the emergency operations center and the other county emergency facilities the county's study names could keep their lights, cooling and radios running. At a shelter, the equipment is sized only for people evacuated because of an incident at the data center, not for hurricane sheltering. The equipment sits at the emergency facility, behind that facility's meter. The utility owns it, or the developer leases it to the county, or it is given to the county with money set aside to maintain it.

items.name: Dark fiber to schools, colleges and clinics
items.hnote: Private agreement between the developer and a community group; the county is not a party.
items.evText: Model text written; not yet reviewed by a lawyer
items.lead: If your school, college or clinic is near the route, the developer may offer it fiber strands directly, under a private agreement. County-run buildings, including county libraries, cannot receive them this way. This does not bring internet service to your home.

items.sec: Private agreement (Model CBA Art. V); on county land, Module M3, Part 2
items.name: Civic Compute Allocation
items.vsub: Condition: the signer must own the computers or commit cloud capacity
items.hnote: Private agreement between the developer and a community group; the county is not a party. On county-owned land, the county as landowner may take it as rent in kind.
items.evText: Model text written; not yet reviewed by a lawyer
items.lead: Where the agreement chooses computing time, a state college, university or other institution that already runs computing hosts it, for residents, students, researchers, nonprofits and small businesses, for coursework, research or public data services.
